content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline specification is ready for review—no application code has been written yet.

- Feature directory: [specs/001-manage-bookmarks](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks)
- Specification: [spec.md](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/spec.md)
- Quality checklist: [requirements.md](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/checklists/requirements.md)
- Validation: All 16 quality checks passed; no unresolved clarifications.

The initial scope is a private, single-user bookmark library with CRUD operations, tags, search, filtering, sorting, duplicate warnings, persistence, and keyboard accessibility. Accounts, synchronization, sharing, import/export, folders, and browser extensions are deferred.

This artifact follows the [speckit-specify workflow](/work/.agents/skills/speckit-specify/SKILL.md).

Please approve the specification or tell me what you’d like changed. Once approved, I’ll create the implementation plan for the next review gate.

Thanks — this is a solid start and most of it matches what I picture: saving links, finding them by search and tags, sorting, editing, deleting, the duplicate warning, and keeping everything between sessions. That all reads right.

Two things give me pause, though, because they're part of what I mean by "save and manage":

1. **Typing in the title myself for every link.** When I paste a web address, I really expect the app to pull in the page's title (and ideally a short description) on its own, so saving is quick. Having to hand-type a title every single time would make saving a chore, which works against the main point of the app. I saw that automatic page info is listed as excluded — I'd like it back in.

2. **A "read later" idea.** A big reason I save links is to come back to them, and I'd want to mark some as "to read" and then see just those in one place (and mark them done). Right now there's no way to separate the stuff I still need to get to from everything else.

Everything else in the excluded list I'm fine setting aside for now. Could you fold those two back into the spec? Once that's in, I think this is ready for the next step.

The specification now includes both requested capabilities:

- Automatic title and description retrieval after entering a URL, with editable results, progress feedback, and manual fallback.
- Persistent Untracked, To Read, and Read states, plus a dedicated Read Later view where items can be completed without removing them from the library.
- Updated user stories, edge cases, requirements, entities, scope, and measurable success criteria.

Review the revised [specification](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/spec.md). The [quality checklist](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/checklists/requirements.md) still passes all 16 checks with no unresolved clarifications.

The revision follows the [speckit-specify workflow](/work/.agents/skills/speckit-specify/SKILL.md). If you confirm this version, I’ll move to the implementation-plan gate.

Both changes are exactly what I was after — pasting a link and having the title and description come in on their own (still editable, with a manual fallback when a page won't cooperate), and a proper "read later" list where I can mark things To Read and then Read without them vanishing from my library. That covers the two gaps I raised, and the rest reads the way I'd expect.

This version looks good to me — go ahead and move on to the implementation plan.

content:
The implementation plan is ready for review. No tasks or application code have been created yet.

Key decisions:

- Single TypeScript application using React/Vite and Express.
- Local SQLite persistence through `better-sqlite3`.
- Security-constrained metadata retrieval with SSRF protection, redirect validation, and strict time/size limits.
- URL-backed Library and Read Later view state.
- Vitest, Testing Library, Supertest, and workspace-matched Playwright 1.61.0.
- One production process on `0.0.0.0:4000`.

Artifacts:

- [Implementation plan](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/plan.md)
- [Research decisions](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/research.md)
- [Data model](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/data-model.md)
- [OpenAPI contract](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/contracts/openapi.yaml)
- [Validation quickstart](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/quickstart.md)

The OpenAPI contract parses and passes structural linting. The constitution check also passes. The plan follows the [speckit-plan workflow](/work/.agents/skills/speckit-plan/SKILL.md).

Please approve the plan or request changes. After approval, I’ll generate the dependency-ordered implementation tasks.

This is more technical than I can fully judge, but from what I can follow it covers everything we agreed on — saving links with the title and description filled in automatically (and safely, without reaching into places it shouldn't), the Read Later list, searching, tagging, sorting, editing, deleting, and keeping all of it saved between restarts. content:
Implemented the complete bookmark manager. All 68 tasks are finished.

Key capabilities include automatic metadata retrieval with secure fallback, Read Later, search and multi-tag filtering, sorting, editing, duplicate handling, confirmed deletion, SQLite persistence, responsive styling, and keyboard accessibility.

Validation passed:

- 165 unit, component, and integration tests
- 18 desktop/mobile Playwright scenarios
- WCAG AA accessibility checks
- 1,000-bookmark performance targets
- Production-process restart persistence
- TypeScript, ESLint, clean install, and production build

Open the application at **http://maker:4000**.

See the [validation report](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/validation.md), [completed task list](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/tasks.md), and [final screenshot](/work/prototypes/final-library.png). Implementation followed the [speckit-implement workflow](/work/.agents/skills/speckit-implement/SKILL.md).

I took the running app for a spin, and everything I care about works the way I hoped:

- Saving a link stores it and it stays in my library.
- Search finds things and ignores capitalization (searching "EXAMPLE" found "Example Site", and a nonsense term correctly returns nothing).
- Filtering by tag and sorting by title both behave.
- The Read Later view shows only what I've marked "to read," and when I mark something Read it drops out of that view but stays in my full library — exactly the behavior I asked for.
- Saving the same address again warns me it's already there instead of silently duplicating.
- Deleting removes it for good.

The automatic title/description fetch is built as a best-effort feature with the manual fallback we agreed on, which is fine by me. This does what I set out to build — I'm happy with it.
